# Benchmark report

These are display-fidelity and frame-behaviour measurements of the benchmark subject named under each result. They are not claims about geometric accuracy; the mathematical tolerances belong to the shared numeric policy (libviprs/pvec#1, P1.2), and this report cites none.

## Real hardware (renderer-keyed baselines)

Stroke pipeline through the buffer pool, 1e6 segments per frame as ten 100k-segment ranges (ten draw calls), 1600x1000 css px at dpr 2, 60 s of rAF frames after a 3 s warm-up. Each row comes from the result file named in its last column; the pixel hash of the fixed snapshot scene is stored per renderer in `bench/baselines/renderer-baselines.json`. The CPU column is JavaScript submit time per frame; the GPU column is the timer-query time where the engine offers one. A 120 Hz display makes the frame interval 8.3 ms, so the interval is capped by the display, not by the work.

### The same scene through the wired layer

The same 1e6 segments in ten style groups (ten draw calls), drawn by `createPVecLayer` on a real MapLibre map with the stand-in cursor (real `.pvec` strokes come with the shared decoder), panned every frame, 60 s after a 3 s warm-up, in the same browser session as the row above. Render CPU is the JavaScript time inside `layer.render`; frame interval is the time between map renders. Settle is from `addLayer` until the pool has uploaded all of it (at most `uploadBudgetBytes` a frame) and every range draws. State diffs come from a separate 400-frame run with the guard's debug diff on.

| renderer | engine | frame p50/p95/max (ms) | frames over 20 ms | draw calls | render CPU p50/p95/max (ms) | GPU frame p50 (ms) | settle (frames / ms) | largest upload in a frame (MiB) | state diffs | errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M5, Unspecified Version) | chromium 149.0.7827.55 | 10.1 / 11 / 13.3 | 0 of 6090 | 10 | 0.1 / 0.1 / 0.2 | 18.8 | 15 / 193 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| Apple GPU | webkit 26.5 | 17 / 18 / 20 | 0 of 3601 | 10 | 0 / 1 / 2 | no timer query | 14 / 290 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| ANGLE (Intel, Mesa Intel(R) Graphics (ADL GT2), OpenGL ES 3.2) | chromium 130.0.6723.31 | 118.8 / 138.4 / 3009.2 | 451 of 451 | 10 | 0.6 / 0.7 / 2081.5 | 70.0 | 18 / 2280 | 4 | 0 | 0 |

The state guard used to read the GL state back every frame, and in Chromium the first `getParameter` waits for the GPU (11 ms of render CPU on the M5, about 5 ms on the Intel part). It now reads the state once to seed a shadow kept by the context's setters, so a steady-state frame does no blocking reads (#96); the debug diff still queries. The pool kept to its upload budget on all three.

### arm64 Linux, software GL (not GPU numbers)

The same raw run and layer run in a linux/arm64 container on an Apple Silicon Mac under Docker Desktop. Docker Desktop passes no GPU into a container, so Chromium drew with SwiftShader on the CPU (4 cpus, 4 GB), at dpr 1 (the GPU rows use dpr 2) because software drawing of the 1e6-segment scene already costs seconds a frame. These rows say the harness, the pool and the wired layer work on arm64 Linux, and what they cost in software. They are not GPU numbers, not tuning input, and they do not stand in for an NVIDIA run or a real-GPU arm64 Linux run: neither was run and neither is claimed ([deferred work](deferred.md)). A frame takes seconds here, so the 60 s loops hold only a handful of frames and the frame percentiles are rough; the layer run's GL state diff covers 5 frames instead of 400.

### Rasters through the wired layer

Scans of A0 at 400 dpi (18724 by 13244 px, 512 px tiles, seven levels) over the 1e6-segment stroke scene, drawn by `createPVecLayer` on a real MapLibre map with the stand-in cursor and a fixture provider in place of the pvec-wasm raster exports. The tiles are the pinned ones of `bench/hw/raster-tiles.json` (one per codec variant and tile size, built by `tools/raster-bench-tiles.sh`), decoded by the shipped decode worker with `createImageBitmap` and uploaded under the 4 MiB and 2 ms budget. The map pans and breathes its zoom by 0.8 of a level every frame, 60 s after a 3 s warm-up, so levels change and decodes run while the frames are timed. Upload counts run from the first frame after `addLayer`, so the fill of the scene is in them. Render CPU is the JavaScript time inside `layer.render`, split in two populations: steady frames (no tile uploaded) carry the budget of ADR 0009, 1.5 ms at the 95th percentile on every real renderer (the mean where the timer resolves 1 ms or coarser, which is WebKit's), and frames that upload a tile are held to one rule: none takes longer than one 60 fps frame (16.7 ms) and none uploads more than the byte budget plus one tile (the p95, the count and the maximum are recorded). ADR 0005's 1 ms stays the pipeline's number. Every row is from the result file in its last column and says which renderer and arch produced it.

The software GL rows (SwiftShader on the CPU, a linux container, no GPU) are relative costs. They say the page, the decode worker and the layer work there and what a frame costs in software; they are not GPU numbers, they are not tuning input, and no budget or frozen value reads from them. The frame counts are low because software drawing of the 1e6-segment scene takes seconds a frame.

## Real pvec evaluator and real .pvec bytes

- `spikes/pvec-real/results.json`: chromium 130.0.6723.31, linux/x64 container, `libviprs/pvec` `ab3c2cf`, ABI version 2
- module 716752 bytes, compile 46.3 ms, instantiate 0.4 ms
- the docker host was shared and loaded while this ran, so every time here is an upper bound and only the shape is a result
- the subject is the shipped evaluator through the packed binding; the arrays are views over linear memory, nothing is copied

### Evaluation cost per named fixture

### Tier 0 stream and spatial directory (ABI 2)

The files are the corpus entries written with a spatial directory and one Tier 0 block per leaf. Entries are what the stream returns for a window; uncovered is what `query_viewport` returns for it less the entries (the advanced curves, which are in no leaf, and every entity of a leaf with no Tier 0 block). Missing is entries plus uncovered less the entity count of the window, so 0 means the audit loses nothing. Previews are checked one way: every point of a tight reference tessellation of the curve is within the declared error of the preview polyline.
